$comment: BSC TESTNET deploy params (2026-09-18). Cloned from testnet-dev, paired with
config/networks.bsc-testnet.json. Lead decisions of 2026-09-18 are applied:
redeemDelay/minRedeemDelay  KEPT at the testnet values -- the delay is a mainnet concern.
schedule 3600/600           KEPT -- this is testnet.
executorSlippageBps 5000    KEPT DELIBERATELY as a wide ceiling, the same posture as the
previous deployments. Measured on the PRUV fork: this band lets a 49% shortfall settle and
refuses 51% (docs/planning/pruv-fork-findings.md section 4). It is immutable, so MAINNET
must revisit it once Pruv's fee behaviour is known -- on testnet a wide ceiling only means
fewer spurious aborts while the vault pays 1:1 and charges nothing.
fees                        NON-ZERO on this instance, so the fee paths are exercised on
staging: 50 bps subscribe-cancel, 50 bps redeem-cancel, 25 bps redemption. REXPrimary
hardcodes feeCapBps = 200, so all three must stay at or under 2%.
**HOME USDC IS 18-DECIMAL HERE.** Derryl's 2026-09-18 FakeUSDC set makes the BSC leg 18 dp to
match mainnet, so every amount denominated in HOME USDC changes scale: minSub and
launchpadMinimum are 20e18, not 20e6. minRedeem does NOT move -- it is wRWA (ADR-026 D2) and
TREX01 is 6 dp on all three chains. Getting this backwards is silent: 20e6 at 18 dp is two
hundredths of a microdollar, so every batch would clear the minimum instantly and the
accrual path would never be reachable.
Both values stay whole micro-units (multiples of 1e12), which ADR-028 D5 requires of anything
that can reach a batch total.
minSub/minRedeem 20         KEPT -- they are what makes ADR-027's accrual path observable.
launchpadPeriod 86400       WIDENED from 3600. The window is the only time deposits are
accepted and closing under launchpadMinimum is TERMINAL (deploy 0xAEf07202 died that way),
so it must outlast whatever we are waiting on -- here, FakeUSDC arriving on BSC.
timeouts                    KEPT as testnet-dev.
feeRecipient                stays ${DEPLOYER_ADDRESS} on testnet.
ADR-030 D5 bounds the delay: redeemDelay and minRedeemDelay stay below
epochDuration - schedule.windowLength, and below pruvExecutor.redeemFulfillTimeout.
The contracts block keeps the PRUV pair and points homeWrwaRoute at BSC's synthetic TREX01
route. Every BSC address was read on chain on 2026-09-18 (both tokens 6-decimal, both routes
scale() == 1, and both routes enrolled with PRUV domain 7336 in BOTH directions).
The four PER-FUND external addresses. Duplicated in config/networks.json for the default
fund only (see its defaultFund note); the deploy scripts read them HERE and fail loud on
drift. fundWrwaRoute is the PRUV (collateral) leg, homeWrwaRoute the Sepolia (synthetic)
leg of the same route pair -- both replaced by Derryl's 2026-08-24 fee=0 redeploy.
Verbatim REXPrimary constructor args, minus the 4 external-contract params + pruvDomain (all
resolved from config/networks.json: usdc/mailbox/usdcRoute/wrwaRoute, and fund.hyperlaneDomain
for pruvDomain); ADR-025 dropped the keeper param entirely (see the schedule block below).
minSub: USDC base units (6dp). 20000000 = 20 USDC (Lead, 2026-09-09), raised from 0. It is the
per-BASKET minimum a subscribe batch must reach before it bridges, NOT a per-user ticket
(ADR-025 rulings 8-9). At 0 the accrual/release path was never exercised on testnet.
launchpadStart: SECONDS-FROM-DEPLOY delay, NOT an absolute Unix timestamp -- the constructor
reverts InvalidLaunchpadConfig if launchpadStart < block.timestamp, so a committed absolute
value would go stale between commit and deploy. The deploy script must compute the real ctor
arg as (deploy-block timestamp + this value), the same pattern the Forge tests use
(block.timestamp + 1 in REXPrimary.lifecycle.t.sol / REXPrimary.parallel.t.sol).
launchpadPeriod: seconds the launchpad stays open to gather launchpadMinimum. 3600 = 1 hour on
testnet-dev (Lead, 2026-09-09); closeLaunchpad reverts LaunchpadNotClosed until
launchpadStart + this elapses, so a 1-day value put the first epoch a day out before the
cadence was even counted. config-values.md section 5 leaves the product value unresolved.
launchpadMinimum: USDC base units; below this at close -> LaunchpadFail + full refund.
20000000 = 20 USDC. NOT a free choice: the constructor reverts InvalidLaunchpadConfig when
launchpadMinimum < minSub (REXPrimary.sol:225), because a launchpad that closes below the
batch minimum could never bridge what it raised. So this tracks minSub and must be raised
with it. OPERATIONAL CONSEQUENCE: at least this much must actually be deposited before
closeLaunchpad, or the fund enters LaunchpadFail and refunds everyone. It was 0 on every
earlier deploy, which is why the constraint never showed up until 2026-09-09.
cancelFeeBps: subscription-cancel fee after freeCancelPeriod (ADR-017), bps of 10000. 0 = testnet-dev
permissive default (config-values.md section 6 suggests 50bps for a real launch, not yet Final).
feeRecipient: testnet-dev reuses the single deploy-EOA placeholder (see roles.$comment).
Verbatim SC3Params (contracts/src/REXPrimary.sol) minus `navOracle` (deploy-resolved, see the
top-level $comment). All timeouts/windows in seconds, fees in bps of 10000.
minRedeem: **wRWA share units** (SC11 / ADR-026), Pruv's minimum redemption batch. NOT USDC --
the gate is `rb.netIn >= minRedeem`, share-count against share-count, which is what lets
initiateSubEpoch read no NAV at all. Reading this as USDC would set it ~1e6 wrong and
nothing would revert: the batch would simply accrue instead of bridging. 20000000 = 20 wRWA
(wRWA is 6dp on home, asserted at deploy), set 2026-09-09 alongside minSub.
redeemCancelFeeBps: redeem-side cancel fee. 0 = testnet-dev permissive (config-values.md
section 6 suggests 10-25bps for a real launch, not yet Final).
redemptionFeeBps: charged on total redeem proceeds at claim (ADR-014). 0 = testnet-dev
permissive (config-values.md section 6 suggests 50bps for a real launch, not yet Final).
redeemFulfillTimeout: seconds before an unfulfilled redeem batch may abortRedeem (ADR-009/012).
950400 = 11 days -- home MUST EXCEED the executor copy (SC13 D12): the home copy waits on a
full round trip, the executor only on its own leg (indicative home-side copy vs the
executor's authoritative one, shared-v1.6).
windDownWindow: seconds redeem stays open after triggerWindDown before triggerShutDown (SC6b).
777600 = 9 days (matches the Forge test default).
subFulfillTimeout: seconds after a subscribe batch BRIDGES before `recoverStuckBatch` may
declare it dead and release its stranded residual (M-1). A bridge-liveness deadline, NOT an
accrual cap -- ADR-027 retired those, and this took over `maxSubWait`'s second job.
MUST EXCEED pruvExecutor.subFulfillTimeout and is deliberately NOT a mirror of it: the
executor times the OUTBOUND leg only, while this one waits on a full round trip (bridge out,
vault deposit, wRWA back).
259200 = 3 days. Sized from OBSERVED latency, not from the old maxSubWait: a return leg lagged
~1 day in 2026-09, and firing early is not a delay but a LOSS -- recoverStuckBatch flips the
batch to Settled with returnedAmount 0, which zeroes every subscriber's claim irreversibly and
permanently blocks the genuine return. 3h (the first value tried here) sat inside the observed
range and would have done exactly that.
SC9 NavReporter constructor param. heartbeatSeconds <= NavOracleConsumer.stalenessWindow so
nav() cannot go stale between real setValue moves (ADR-004 A1; config-values.md sections 63/68).
1800 = 30 min = 0.5x the live testnet 1h stalenessWindow. mainnet value = risk review.
mailbox/homeDomain/rwaConversion come from config/networks.json; consumer is passed at deploy
time (the live NavOracleConsumer address, config/deployments.json).
TODO before deploy: redeemDelay, minRedeemDelay and executorSlippageBps are placeholders
borrowed from testnet-dev. See this file's header.
Verbatim PruvExecutor constructor args minus the 6 external-contract/network params
(mailbox/wrwaRoute/usdc/usdcRoute/rwaToken from config/networks.json's fund entry, homeDomain from
home.hyperlaneDomain). Timeouts in seconds, bps of 10000.
subFulfillTimeout: deadline on a recorded-but-unexecuted subscribe leg before abortDeposit
(ADR-015 D9). 3600 = 1 hour (matches the Forge test default).
executorSlippageBps: floor on the vault's output, as drift against the LOCAL fund-chain
rwaConversion.value() -- no longer vs the bridged navAtInitiate (ADR-026 W3). 5000 = 50%,
mandated by ADR-026 decision 5 and raised from 100 on 2026-09-09. It is the ONLY guard on
vault output in either path (there is no separate zero check), so it must never be 1e4: at
1e4 the floor computes to zero and a 0-share deposit or 0-USDC redeem would be accepted and
latched. The constructor rejects >= 1e4. 50% keeps a catastrophe guard while never firing on
Pruv's exit fee or on rounding -- at 100 it would have reverted executeRedeem every time if
that fee exceeded 1%.
redeemFulfillTimeout: issuer fulfillment deadline gating abortRedeem, executor-side authoritative
copy (shared-v1.6). 864000 = 10 days -- home MUST EXCEED the executor copy (SC13 D12), so
rexPrimary.sc3Params.redeemFulfillTimeout above is 950400, not this value.
NO reuseAddress here, on purpose. Every deploy since 1.1.0 REUSED the Sepolia consumer
0x9a42404134f1001d259fC979c2471D60BB989eB8 (removed from this file: 0x9a42404134f1001d259fC979c2471D60BB989eB8)
because the home chain never changed. BSC is a new home chain, so that address has no code there
and DeployHome.s.sol:93 would refuse it outright. A fresh NavOracleConsumer is deployed here --
and per that script's own warning, a new consumer FORCES a new NavReporter on PRUV, because
NavReporter.consumer is immutable.
reporter: the NavReporter deployed for THIS home chain on 2026-09-18, paired with the BSC
NavOracleConsumer 0xCaaCB584ba961b8363BC7B59D3C44cE6d892D105. NavReporter.consumer is immutable, so this
pair is fixed: a different consumer would need a different reporter. Set before
`ops post-deploy` runs, or the consumer enrolls a sender that never pokes it and every
poke() from the real reporter is rejected -- silent, no revert at deploy time.
a sender that never pokes it, and every poke() from the real reporter would be rejected.
Access-control addresses applied post-deploy (owner/guardian are REXPrimary; reporter is
NavOracleConsumer.enrollReporter's bytes32 sender). testnet-dev collapses these to ONE
DEPLOYER_ADDRESS in the environment before running; no default is invented here.
owner: Ownable2Step owner (REXPrimary) -- defaults to the deploying address at construction;
restated here so later deploy steps (setGuardian/ownership transfer) have one
source of truth.
guardian: REXPrimary.setGuardian target -- MANDATORY post-deploy step (config-values.md
section 7): the pool launches with guardian == address(0) (pause disabled) until this call.
PER DEPLOYMENT, not a fixed role: NavReporter's `consumer` is immutable, so a new
NavOracleConsumer forces a new NavReporter, and this value MUST be updated to the newly
deployed reporter BEFORE `ops post-deploy` runs -- otherwise the consumer enrolls the wrong
sender and every poke() is rejected. (Before SC9 there was no reporter contract and this
reused the deploy EOA as a stand-in; that is no longer the topology.)
TODO before deploy: epochDuration and windowLength are the 1h/10m test cadence, not production.
ADR-025 / RULING 8: the epoch calendar, deployed as its own EpochSchedule contract and passed
to REXPrimary via SC3Params. DeployHome derives epochStart itself as (launchpadStart +
launchpadPeriod + epochDuration) -- at LEAST one full epochDuration after the launchpad closes,
not the close instant itself: closeLaunchpad neither advances currentEpochId nor touches
lastClosedPeriod, so epochStart == launchpadClose would make periodOf(now) already 1 > 0 the
moment the launchpad closes, letting the first depositor after close immediately trigger epoch
1 -- the exact defect the schedule design exists to remove. Only epochDuration is config here;
epochStart is never read as a raw value, so an operator cannot re-introduce the instant-close
by editing config alone.
epochDuration is 30 days in PRODUCTION. This file is testnet-dev and runs 3600 = ONE HOUR
(Lead, 2026-09-09) -- what David asked for during testing. At the production cadence the
first epoch could not close until ~31 days after deploy, so the gate would be unobservable.
Change this and maxSubWait/maxRedeemWait TOGETHER: DeployHome and postDeploy both assert
the caps strictly exceed it.
